CCST 500.title: Seminar in Interdisciplinary Frameworks in Museum and Curatorial Studies
CCST 500.description: Theoretical and historical foundations of visual representations and expressive culture. It explores the history of museums and galleries, and changes in the meaning of art and material culture as debates about cultural property intensify.

CCST 501.title: Seminar in Contemporary Contextual Issues for Museums and Curatorial Practice
CCST 501.description: An examination of broad social and political issues that confront curators and museum professionals who construct representations in museums, art galleries and other sites of public display.

CCST 502.title: Case Studies in Museum and Gallery Exhibitions
CCST 502.description: A case study approach to analyzing museum and gallery exhibitions that are historically significant either because they raised issues and stimulated public debate, or because of radical features that proved influential on subsequent exhibitions. Course not offered every year.

CCST 503.title: Graduate Practicum in Critical and Curatorial Studies
CCST 503.description: Practical on-site teamwork to produce exhibitions or other public displays in a museum, gallery, or alternative situation, offering opportunities for comparison, collaboration, and interdisciplinarity.

CCST 504.title: Major Paper in Critical and Curatorial Studies
CCST 504.description: To graduate, students must produce a major paper from the ideas and research which generate the exhibition in the practicum.
